summary: Architecture-only phase determining, from evidence across twelve completed PCAE initiatives (105, 106, 110, 118-125, 127-129, 130, 131-132, 133, 134, 135, 136, 137), whether the recurring Architecture -> Contract Freeze -> Implementation -> Independent Verification -> Repository-Wide Hardening -> Certification sequence is a genuine reusable governance pattern or an accidental similarity. Ran seven parallel evidence-gathering passes, one per initiative cluster, each instructed to extract citation-backed facts without drawing the six-stage conclusion; synthesized the conclusion once, across all seven, so no single initiative was treated as sufficient proof. Conclusion: repeatable governance methodology, applied proportionally, not a rigid universal template. A four-stage core (Architecture, Contract Freeze, Implementation, Independent Verification) appears in essentially every initiative studied; Repository-Wide Hardening and Certification are conditional additions reserved for track-closing, cross-cutting initiatives. Found the pattern independently self-cited within the repository more than once prior to this phase (135A section 18.1 citing Track 134 and Repository Intelligence precedent; 137P modeling itself on 134A/135A; 133E naming a three-stage sub-cycle) -- evidence of a recognized, reused convention rather than coincidental resemblance. Documented which lifecycle stage caught which class of historical defect (Contract Freeze catching design-paraphrase ambiguity in 136D; Independent Verification catching implementation deviations across dozens of paired phases; Repository-Wide Hardening catching cross-track duplication invisible to narrower-scoped stages in 137T and Track 124; Certification catching accumulated-claim drift in 134F, which correctly declined to certify and issued CONDITIONALLY CLOSED instead of a false positive). Also disclosed a scope-boundary finding: the pattern reliably protects the subsystem an initiative builds but does not automatically protect the governance tooling used to run the initiative, evidenced by three recurring finalization/reporting incidents in Track 135 (135D.1, 135H.1, 135H.2.1) that escaped every designated verification stage. No governance rules changed. No contract issued. No production code touched. Runtime remained Observed / observe / unavailable throughout. Recommends 137W (contract freeze), consistent with 137U's own prior recommendation, only if the human authority elects to proceed.
